title: [CQ-M01d] Attempt policy snapshot capture
description:
Objective: Bind each real execution attempt to a durable detached policy configuration identity without rewriting historical attempts.

Deliverable: Have openAttempt derive policy data from daemon task/project state, never a new caller-controlled MCP snapshot argument. New claims capture the effective configuration; strict task requirements cannot weaken after project rollback. Repair/resume keeps the original attempt identity and snapshot unchanged, while a successor generation records a fresh configuration identity. Preserve the existing pure attempt-store legacy behavior for historical/no-task records. Return detached snapshot copies without exposing mutable stored policy objects, and preserve persist-before-publish plus claim compensation on failure.

Existing implementation surfaces / proposed focused tests (maximum five files): packages/moe-daemon/src/state/attemptStore.ts (openAttempt/repairExisting/getAttempt/listAttempts/currentAttempt); packages/moe-daemon/src/state/attemptStore.test.ts; packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/claimNextTask.ts (openClaimAttempt/handBackUnrecordedClaim); packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/claimNextTask.contract.test.ts.

NOT in scope: Session/context receipts, stale-attempt fencing expansion, QA candidate binding, trusted runner evidence, approving the captured revision, or profile activation. Verification (fresh, exit 0): cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test -- --maxWorkers=4. Run in a synchronized isolated copy with native Linux dependencies and Linux-only PATH; preserve the original Windows node_modules and unchanged package-lock.json. Each slice owns its behavior tests, one final verification/adversarial review, and no production activation. This breakdown defines deliverables, not per-task implementation steps.
definitionOfDone: Real open/claim tests persist the derived configuration snapshot and reload it unchanged after daemon restart.
Same-id repair and own-seat resume retain original generation/snapshot despite project changes; a legitimate successor gets a new generation and configuration record.
Returned/opened/listed snapshot objects cannot mutate stored snapshot state through aliasing.
Injected/forged policy inputs are not adopted; strict policy cannot downgrade through a resumed/replaced attempt or current project rollback.
Failed attempt persistence leaves no published attempt and existing claim compensation remains correct; pre-snapshot historical/no-task store behavior stays compatible.
Fresh `cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test -- --maxWorkers=4` exits 0 in the synchronized native-Linux copy, with actual pass/skip counts and output supplied to complete_task.
taskRails: Do not enable verified-local or claim approval, runner trust, hardware/isolation certification, or verified completion from a configuration snapshot.
Do not edit packages/moe-daemon/src/delivery/acceptance.test.ts or weaken existing held-out delivery assertions; add focused tests for new behavior.
No direct .moe edits or Git writes; wrappers own landing. Keep each implementation plan within five source/test files and normal sizing limits.
